subject: Meteorology
title: The Hygrometer
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Hygrometer usable.

hook.text: Leonardo da Vinci designed an early hygrometer around 1480—using a ball of wool that gained weight as humidity rose.

buildup.text: Other early designs used hair, seaweed, or catgut—materials that change length with moisture in predictable ways.

discovery.text: Horace-Bénédict de Saussure built the hair hygrometer in 1783—human hair stretches about 2.5% from dry to saturated air.

twist.text: The psychrometer (wet-and-dry bulb) became the standard—evaporative cooling on the wet bulb indicates relative humidity.

climax.text: Humidity measurements turned rain forecasting from guesswork into science—moisture in the air could finally be tracked.

punchline.text: From wool to hair to thermometer pairs—measuring the invisible moisture.

quiz.question: How does a psychrometer measure humidity?
options: By comparing wet and dry bulb temperatures
